Topic1.Title: Bike Security and Theft Reduction Update
Topic1.Summary: Staff from Transportation and Mobility and the Boulder Police Department presented the completed work of a council priority project to reduce bike theft and improve bike security. Bike thefts fell 14% year-over-year through August 2026, and the recovery rate of stolen bikes rose to 13%, putting the team on track for its goal of a 10% reduction. Key efforts included bike registration through Bike Index, public education on proper locking, short-term bike parking guidance for businesses, rack replacements, and data-driven targeted bike theft operations. Council members asked for full-year theft figures, raised concerns about police staffing and the project's future, and discussed e-bike theft and bike shop registration.

Topic2.Title: Wildfire Ready 2030 Framework and Home Hardening Implementation Hub
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the Wildfire Ready 2030 framework, which organizes about 137 projects under four strategies, 25 programs, and 10 tier-one priorities focused on reducing risk to life safety. The team introduced the Wildfire Ready Action Hub to help residents assess their risk and take practical steps to harden their homes, and the Wildland Urban Interface Risk Index to prioritize resources across 12 western sections. Fourteen performance measures were set through 2030, such as 55% of homes receiving detailed home assessments and 20% being hardened, and staff proposed about $1.85 million in additional 2027 enhancements. Council provided feedback on accelerating home hardening, consolidating building standards, improving evacuation and recovery planning, and considering policy options such as rental license requirements, with staff to return with updates in spring 2027.
